newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends higher but fails to match NY pace.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends higher but fails to match NY pace.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures managed to claw back most of the ground lost during Wednesday's session but failed to keep pace with the reignited New York market.
London ended mostly firmer across the board and benchmark July managed to recover from a low of $2,030, $45 down on the day, to stand at $2,090 at the close.
Traders said origin sellers were capping gains at around the $2,100 mark.

"The origins are selling a little bit at $2,100 so it's holding in a range and settling down after the last move -- whereas New York has a mind of its own. You've got to stand back and let it go," said one.
Arabica prices reignited after news that the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) agreed to extend export quotas for another 12 months.

The ACPC agreed to limit total exports by its 14 members to 52.75 million (60 kg) bags for the 12 months starting from July 1. The volume is roughly the same as the limit applied under current curbs expiring June 30.
But London traders said the news had been largely factored into the robustas market, adding that there had been limited interest in the arbitrage against New York.
Prices could now consolidate or even drift lower but would still depend on the gyrations of New York to a certain extent.
"I think in London the funds have done what they're going to do to it," the trader said.
"They're quite a bit long now...you'll have to go up another $100 before they'll start buying again."
Volume amounted to 5,409 lots, more than half of which was in July.
